title: Nightshift triage heuristics & quick experiments
content:
Context:
Quick, lightweight nightshift cheat-sheet for triage and small experiments when p99 starts to creep or an odd kernel hang shows up. This is intentionally compact — notes to self more than polished runbook.

Goal: reduce time-to-hypothesis for common perf regressions (micro-batching, kv cache growth, cuda context thrash). Prefer quick measurable changes + rollback.

Today (notes):
- 23:10 observed p99 jump ~+120ms across a handful of routes (mainly long-history chat routes).
- Symptoms: intermittent queue backlog, worker spin ups, one-ish host with high GPU mem (90% pct).
- Quick check: dashboard -> route=chat-long, model=gpt-open-16b-qa, time window=23:00-23:12 -> saw 12 spikes.
- Correlated with a few large requests from internal QA (session ids start with qa-).

Immediate triage steps (3-step routine):
1) Filter + isolate
   - narrow to single host: use trace-id from first spike -> host ip 10.23.9.42
   - check host SRE dashboard: memory, cpu, disk io, GPU mem timeline.
   - run: ssh runtime-10-23-9-42 && nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0 | tail -n +1
   - quick look at docker stats: docker ps -> docker exec -it <container> ps aux | head

2) Snapshot runtime state
   - dump KV cache size (endpoint exposed): curl -s http://localhost:9800/metrics | grep kv_cache_entries
   - if kv_cache_entries > 150k then hypothesis A: cache blowup from long chat histories -> try TTL prune on that host (toggle local flag for now).
   - collect kernel logs: sudo journalctl -u runtime -n 500 > /tmp/runtime-journal-$(date +%s).log

3) Quick mitigation + observe (10m window)
   - if queue length > 30: temporarily increase workers by +1 (scale override) for that host, monitor latency.
   - if GPU mem > 88% and kv_cache_entries high: restart local runtime worker (graceful): curl -X POST http://localhost:9800/admin/graceful-restart and watch for cache warmup time.
   - if problem disappears: revert experiment to config repo, create follow-up PR to add TTL default for <route>.

Hypotheses to test (ordered cheap -> expensive):
- H1: One-off long-history chats (no prefix caching) cause KV cache growth and xfer thrash -> test by pruning histories > 2048 tokens for 30m and watching mem.
- H2: Continuous batching heuristics misestimate idle windows when traffic is bursty -> simulate burst with stress tool and compare p99 with batching disabled.
- H3: CUDA context churn when worker restart collides with kernel warm-up -> instrument with small counter metric for kernel-loads-per-minute and correlate with restarts.

Quick commands / snippets I keep forgetting:
- tail runtime logs across host: ssh host && sudo journalctl -u runtime -f | sed -n '1,200p'
- dump GPU mem histogram: python3 -c "import gpustat, pprint; pprint.pprint(gpustat.new_query().jsonified())"
- request replay (safe): curl -X POST https://replay.redwood.ai/api/replay -d '{\"trace_id\":\"<trace>\"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

Micro experiments to run when time allows (label -> metric -> target):
- microbatch-window: reduce window from 80ms -> 60ms for route chat-long -> expect p99 down 20-40ms, throughput neutral.
- kv-ttl: add per-route TTL 30m for chat-long -> expect GPU mem drop, cache hit rate drop smallish (<5%).
- batching-threshold: lower min-batch to 2 for low QPS routes to avoid over-aggregation -> observe p50 & p95.

Notes to self / things to record in ticket:
- Keep prefetch flag changes reversible via feature flag.
- If rolling restart required, do host-by-host with 5m stagger to avoid global cold misses.
- Check PR #1427 for kernel change that touched alloc heuristics (might be root cause).

Open questions for oncall handoff:
- Was there a new deploy around 22:50? who deployed? (check deploy logs / circleci).
- Any recent quantization profile updates for gpt-open-16b-qa? (ask model-onboarding).

Follow-ups (create issues):
- RINF-2107: Investigate KV eviction heuristics and default TTL per route (assigned to Mina).
- RINF-2130: Add kernel-load metric + alert when restarts correlate with p99 increase (Sanjay to own).

Housekeeping / TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Draft short runbook section for 'kv_cache runaway' with exact commands and rollback steps.
- [ ] Add quick dashboard widget for per-host kv_cache_entries.
- [ ] Run microbatch-window experiment on staging and log results (date planned: 2024-11-12).
- [ ] Review PR 1427 diff and annotate possible risky lines.

Random mental notes (messy):
- fuzzy thought: maybe the continuous-batcher should prefer smaller batches for users with long histories; small speedup might avoid big cache pressure.
- note: watch for pattern where chaos happens ~30-40 minutes after large QA sweep (maybe session reuse issue).

If I wake up later:
- re-check 00:30 metrics, if still flaky escalate to oncall SRE and trigger cluster-wide cache prune flag (manual toggle in ops console).

-----
End of night scratchpad. Use this to populate RINF tickets with a minimal reproduction steps + logs. Keep it terse and actionable.
